First, create() checks the capacity range (1–300) itself. That business rule belongs to the domain, in the Course aggregate. Second, toCourse() turns a TypeORM CourseEntity into a domain Course. This entity-to-domain mapping is persistence work for a repository or adapter in the infrastructure layer. Third, the service writes TypeORM queries directly (findOne with where id, find with where published true, plus create and save). Those queries belong behind an infrastructure repository. The NestJS habit of injecting a Repository<CourseEntity> into a service is common, so treating that alone as a violation is debatable.
